newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers reports record profits; stock jumps.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers reports record profits; stock jumps.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. Tuesday reported record profits for the latest quarter, despite the negative effect of a strong dollar on the health and personal care product maker's foreign businesses.
Net income jumped to $810 million or 81 cents a share on sales of $4.04 billion in the first quarter vs. earnings of $726 million or 72 cents a share on sales of $3.66 billion in a year earlier.
Following the news, Bristol-Myers' stock rose $1.875 to $61.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
The New York-based company said U.S. sales rose 11 percent, while international sales were up 9 percent, or 14 percent excluding the unfavourable currency fluctuations.
"Our first-quarter performance establishes a solid growth track at Bristol-Myers Squibb as we begin 1997," said Charles A. Heimbold, Jr., chairman and chief executive officer.
Pharmaceutical product sales rose 12 percent from a year ago, as sales of the cholesterol lowering drug Pravachol -- the company's largest selling product -- soared 48 percent.
Consumer product sales rose 10 percent, led by gains in sales of hair care products, Herbal Essences and Clairol Hydrience.
Nutritional product sales grew 12 percent, while medical device product sales slipped 1 percent.
